'Compare your ear with the words of the wise and hear my word; and examine your own heart, so that you may know that they are good' (Prov 23:23); this one hears the words of God, the one doing the things commanded by them; 'for not the hearers of the law are righteous before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified' (James 1:22).

'And you also shall write them down for yourself thrice for counsel and knowledge upon the breadth of your heart'; he who broadens his heart through purity will perceive the words of God, both the practical, the natural, and the theological. For all the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: According to the Scripture, the matter is divided quite sharply into the ethical, the natural, and the theological. To the first follows Proverbs, to the second Ecclesiastes, and to the third the Hymns of the Hymns.

Regarding Proverbs 24:8, 26: 'Do not give yourself as a surety, being ashamed of your face'; and 24:27: 'For if you do not have [something] from which to spread [it], the layer under your sides shall be taken.' Those who entertain bad thoughts and thus honor the evil one should strive to whatever power they can through good thoughts to restore the bad ones. For if they are not able to do this, the layer under the sides of the soul—that is, virtue—shall be taken. For this is called the garment of the mind when it stands in righteousness, but it is called a cushion when the rest has fallen due to bad thoughts.

Regarding Proverbs 24:28: 'Do not move the eternal boundaries which your fathers set.' He who moves the boundaries of godliness demonstrates either superstition or impiety, and he who moves the boundaries of courage achieves either rashness or cowardice. Likewise, this should be considered regarding the other virtues, regarding the dogmas, and regarding faith itself. Above all, this must be observed concerning the Holy Trinity; for he who does not theologize divides the Holy Spirit by baptism, and he who names others as gods introduces a crowd of gods.

Regarding Proverbs 23:1: 'If you sit to dine at the table of a powerful man, observe mindfully what is set before you...' and 23:3: 'But if you are more gluttonous, do not desire his delicacies'; for these things possess a false life. For not everyone contains the more mystical intellect of the Scripture. It is necessary that the Divine Scripture be understood mindfully and spiritually; for sensory knowledge according to the history is not true.

Regarding Proverbs 23:6: 'Do not dine with a coarse man'; nor desire his foods; 23:7: 'For in whatever way anyone swallows hair, so he eats and drinks'; 23:8: 'Nor let him be brought to you, and eat your bread with him'; for he will vomit him out and will defile your beautiful words. If the coarse man eats the grain of impiety and drinks lawless wine, one must not dine with him; therefore, it is not right to be impious and lawless, for these vices defile spiritual knowledge. Regarding Proverbs 23:9: 'Say nothing into the ears of a fool'...

Regarding the acquisition of your wise words: 'Say nothing wise,' that is to say, profound and mystical; for it is not fitting to cast pearls before swine. Regarding the boundaries: 'Do not shift the eternal boundaries which your fathers set,' and 'Do not enter the estate of orphans,' for wickedness is that by which they were deprived of their Father in heaven.

Regarding jealousy: 'Let not your heart envy sinners,' but be in the fear of the Lord all your days. Since it is said, 'All turns away from evil by the fear of the Lord' (Proverbs 23:17), it rightly exhorts us to turn away from all evil throughout our whole life.

Regarding offspring: 'If you keep these, you shall have offspring,' and 'your hope shall not be disappointed.' The mind has said that the right reasonings and the spiritual contemplations are offspring. Therefore, the soul is barren which does not have these offspring, which it is nature to bring forth from the spiritual bridegroom.

Regarding drunkenness and fornication: 'Every drunkard and fornicator shall be poor, and shall clothe himself in torn and ragged things.' There is no wedding garment that is torn and ragged. Regarding the mother: 'Listen, son, to the father of him who begot you, and do not despise that your mother has grown old.' One of the elders heard someone saying the soul is the mother of the mind; for this, he says, leads the mind into light through the practical virtues. The 'soul' referred to was the passionate part of the soul, which is divided into spirit and desire. For through courage and temperance, he says, we acquire wisdom and knowledge of God. Courage and temperance are the virtues of spirit and desire.

Regarding wines: 'Not of those who intoxicate with wines? Not of those who track where the drinking takes place?' These wines are from the vine of Sodom. Regarding fellowship: 'Do not get drunk with wine, but converse with righteous men, and converse in your walkings.' The Mind, conversing in walkings, walks worthily of the calling wherewith he was called.

Regarding eyes and cups: 'If you give your eyes to bowls and cups.' Sin resembles a bowl according to thought, and a cup according to energy. Regarding nakedness: 'Later you will walk more naked than the proud.' The proud knock much and do not open the place they knock at. But to the disciples the Lord says, 'Knock and it shall be opened to you' (Matthew 7:7). Regarding the eyes and mouth: 'Your eyes, when they see something foreign, your mouth then will speak.'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Judgment and the Sword of God
english: A scholion: A mind having received an alien thought will meditate on evil logismoi (thoughts). But he who guards himself will inherit life (Prov 26:3).
And it will lie still, just as in the heart of a sea, and just as a pilot in a great swell, being tossed by every wind of instruction (Prov 26:4).
When will the dawn be, so that coming, I may seek with those with whom I will be gathered? The dawn of the soul is the recognition of sin (Prov 26:5).
After steering comes war, but help comes with a deliberative heart. Those shipwrecking regarding faith do not fight against the opposing spirits in war with steering (Prov 26:6).

It is also possible to say this regarding every virtue; for there is also shipwreck regarding temperance, and regarding love, and regarding freedom from greed; and regarding each doctrine, similarly, it becomes a shipwreck according to the catholic and apostolic church. If, however, one must fight against the adversaries after steering, life upon the earth is near to us as a naval battle (Prov 26:7).
Wisdom and good understanding in the gates of the wise (Prov 26:9). The gates of the wise are the practical virtues through which the wisdom of God enters.

Impurity will stain a man like a plague (Prov 26:10), in a day of evil and in a day of tribulation, until it fails away. If vice diminishes virtue, and showing that virtue corrupts vice; this indeed will happen in the age to come, until vice fails away. For it has been set to stain instead of corrupting; but impurity is corrupted, either by practical [discipline] or by the punishment of severity (Prov 26:11).

To rescue those being led unto death and those being driven out to be slain, let him not spare. This is the word for those being made worthy of knowledge and those neglecting instruction, many of whom are led by vice unto death (Prov 26:13).

Eat honey, O son, for it is a good thing, so that your throat may be sweetened (Prov 25:28). He who benefits from the divine writings eats honey; but he who casts out the words from those very things from which even the holy prophets and apostles have received, chews wax. And to eat honey is possible for everyone who wishes, but the wax is for the pure alone (Prov 24:15).

Do not bring near the impious thinking they are righteous, nor be deceived by the fullness of the belly. Do not betray God for the sake of pleasure; for this one is thought to be righteous and will never abandon you (Prov 24:17). If the [man] falls...

Do not rejoice over your enemy, nor exult in his stumbling, for the Lord will see and it will not please him, and he will turn his anger away from him. God indeed turns his anger away from the fallen one having had mercy on him, but he is angry with the one who has become proud over the fall of his enemy.

For everyone who rejoices over a perishing soul is like the devil, who does not want all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. It should be noted, however, that he spoke of a human being here, for whom the Lord has enjoined us to pray in the Gospels (1 Timothy 2:1).

Evil offspring will not be produced, but the light of the ungodly will be extinguished. Bad virtues and doctrines will not be produced—for these are the offspring of the soul—because they do not fear the Lord; but those who are in the fear of the Lord will have offspring all day long, and their hope will not fail.

Fear God, son, and the King, and do not disobey either of them, 'so that they may know you, the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ' (John 4:24). For the ungodly will be extinguished suddenly; and who will know the punishments of both? How then does the Savior say in the Gospels: 'The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son' (John 5:22)? Either punishment is one thing, and judgment is another. Punishment is indeed the deprivation of impassibility and the knowledge of God with bodily distress; but judgment is the distribution of an age according to each of the rational bodies.

The tongue of a king is a sword and not a flesh-wound; and whoever is delivered to it will be crushed, 'and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God' (Ephesians 6:17). The 'not flesh-wound' [refers to] the 'not sensible'. If his anger is sharpened, he consumes men with nerves.

The sword of God consumes the old men who are being corrupted according to the desires of sickness, so that, having laid aside the old man, they may put on the new one created according to God. It rattles the bones of men and burns like a flame, 'for I came to cast fire upon the earth' (Luke 12:49). He is spotless for the pure, the one having been cleansed by the Lord and abstaining from all evil.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Ownership, Stewardship, and the Field of the Mind
english: For I am the most foolish of all men, and there is no human wisdom in me. The Foolish One said this by way of the lack of human wisdom.
Who ascended into heaven and descended? 'No one has ascended into heaven above, except the Son of Man who descended from heaven' (John 3:13).

Who gathered the winds in a bosom? Who wetted water in a garment? Who grasped all the ends of the earth? By what faith or in what way did he gather those 'from the east and the west and the north and the sea' (Ezekiel 38:15) into the knowledge of God and have given to them a spiritual vision to deposit in the virtues? And in another way: Who through true knowledge hid false knowledge? Who deposited true knowledge in the virtues? Who 'from the east and the west and the north and the sea' (Ezekiel 38:15) gathered all the nations, making them dense with the virtues and depositing the heavenly water, the flowing from the spring of life?
Do not add to his words, so that he may not examine you and you become false; for by the law of the Lord, 'it is not permitted to add, and it is not permitted to take away' (Rev 22:18-19).
Make a vain word and a long false word far from me. Make a pseudonymous knowledge far from me.

So that, not being filled, I may not become false and say: 'Who sees me?' Or, being in need, I may steal and swear by the name of God. Lest, he says, being filled, a proud listener of knowledge I become and say: 'No one shall know my wisdom.' Lest, being filled with unapproachable knowledge, I appear to men as a liar, saying such things which those endowed with blood and flesh are not able to know.

And the following is also well-added: 'so that, not being in need, I may not steal and swear by the name of God'; for someone steals foreign theories so that he may fill his mind while starving. But this happened before the coming of the Savior; now Paul says: 'let him who steals steal no longer' (Eph 4:28), but rather let him work righteousness.

so that having acquired knowledge, one may share it with the one in need. For what indeed is that which is not ours, so that we, who have believed in Christ, should steal? For all things are ours, but we belong to Christ, through whom all things came to be, and Christ belongs to God (John 16:15).

He who steals knowledge is not the one taking from the one who previously possessed it, but the one who subtracts knowledge from a false name. For all those who have believed in Christ, receiving insights from the holy prophets and apostles, are not called thieves of others' insights, but rather heirs of ancestral goods.

Do not hand over a servant into the hands of a master, lest he curse you and you be destroyed. Flee, mind, lest you hand over [yourself] to evil again, if 'everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin' (1 John 3:8). And now, the one practicing sin is called sin by the devil.
But those who rebuke [others] will appear better; and a good blessing will come upon them. The good blessing is the intellectual one, which is distinguished from the sensory blessing.

Prepare your works for the exodus and prepare for the field. Our Lord in the Gospels named the world a field; but Solomon now has spoken of the field as the theory of the world. But the field in the Gospels is that of the existing composition of a human soul and body, for it is sensory; whereas the field indicated here is of the mind alone, being intellectual and understood from these words of the world, into which pure hearts enter.

And go after me and you will rebuild your house, 'for a house is built with wisdom' (Prov 24:3); 'but into a poorly-crafted soul wisdom will not enter.' If you leave him, he will become a wasteland and will wither and become abandoned; and the barriers of his stones will be dug up. A barrier is apatheia of the rational soul, established from the practical virtues.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Interpretations of Proverbs
english: Crows, mocking a father and dishonoring a mother in her old age, tore him away from the ravines, and young eagles devoured him.

These crows mystically feed the righteous, but they slaughter the unrighteous, gouging out the eyes of injustice, because they mocked the Father of all, who is God, and they dishonored the ancient knowledge that bore them. Regarding those gouging out the eyes, he called them crows; but regarding those devouring the whole man, he named them eagles, because one believes in a partial purification and the other in a total purification.
If the unpure are standing on the left of the Savior, and the goat leads these, let us hope the goat does not now signify the devil.
The weak will not be able to judge correctly if, by drinking, they forget wisdom.

Give a drink to those in sorrows and let those in pains drink wine, so that they may forget their poverty and may no longer remember their labors; for he who is intoxicated by the potency of the master's house forgets his pains.
Open your mouth and judge justly; but distinguish the poor and the weak. The poor is he who is destitute of knowledge, and the weak is the unpure.

The glory of God hides the Word, but the glory of a king honors commands. He who possesses the glory of God, he called the glory of God, and he who possesses the glory of the heavenly king, he called the glory of a king. For they hide the Word of God within themselves, so that they might not sin and [so that they] might honor the commands through which they act. Often we have noted this: that those possessing virtues or vices are named by the virtues or the vices. Thus, 'The Lord is just and loves justice' [Psalm 11:7] refers to the just, instead of the just ones; and 'The fear of the Lord hates injustice, pride, and arrogance' [Proverbs 8:13], that is, the unjust, the insolent, and the arrogant. And here too, he called the one possessing the glory of God 'the glory of God' and the one possessing the glory of the king 'the glory of a king.' Or perhaps he says 'glory of God' regarding the one glorifying God, and 'glory of a king' regarding the one glorifying the king, so that the saying might be such: the one glorifying God...
one establishes his own mind in righteousness
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Varied Names of the Soul's States
english: impassive
To stand in judgment is not good. Just as cold water is unpleasing to a soul that thirsts, so is a good message from far off the earth, and so is the knowledge of God from the earth pleasant.

Just as if someone were to break open a spring and enjoy the outlet of water, so a just man falls disorderly before the thought of the thoughts of the ungodly; his falls are called such and such, his risings, his seat, his standing; and others his walking and some of his obstacles are named; and others hard and soft and fragrant and sweet and bitter and smooth and straight and crooked; and again some of his are called thorns and briars, others light and darkness and life and death, others diseases and healths; and others again are named falsehood and truth; and many other names the Scripture sets down according to the soul and the thoughts of it.

But what it sets down against it, as it is possible to say a few of many, these are they: mind, soul, heart, man, man, woman, slave, servant, father, son, spirit, eye, mouth, lip, tongue, larynx, belly, bosom, arm, finger, wood, nose, sheep, ram, shepherd; and there are more names of the soul, which it is not possible now to set down because the nature of the scholia does not permit prolixity. There, therefore, a just mind falls before the devil, receiving an unclean thought or a false dogma. And David says: 'Before him shall all those descending into the earth fall' (Ps 102:7); but this fall contains true knowledge and pure thoughts.
Just as a city with its walls cast down and without walls, so a man who does nothing by intention. 'Will' is spoken here for the inclination of the heart toward the better.
Just as a whip to a horse and a goad to a donkey, so a rod chastises the lawless. The rod is now a symbol of punishment.

He who sends a word through a foolish angel makes a dream of his own ways. It is not necessary to give the holy things to dogs, nor to cast pearls before swine (Mt 7:6). Having removed the journey of the legs and the lawlessness from the mouth of the foolish, remove the bad way and make a long distance of false knowledge from it. He who releases a stone from a sling is like one giving glory to a foolish person. Knowledge will not fit a fool and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Virtue, Knowledge, and the Perils of the Soul
english: A stone is worthless in a golden setting.

Much is covered by the flesh of fools, for their ecstasy is crushed. If the ecstasy of fools, by which they were beside themselves for God (cf. Luke 16:15), is crushed, having become pure again, they approach God; for 'all flesh shall see the salvation of God.' One must note here that he named the thickened souls from the evil flesh of fools. So also the Lord says: 'My spirit shall not remain in these men because they are flesh' (cf. Romans 8:3).

Like a dog when it rushes upon its own vomit and becomes loathsome, so a fool, having turned back to his own sin by his own wickedness, is like a dog eating its own vomit after casting away his wickedness and turning again toward it.

Having hidden a sluggish hand in his lap, he will not be able to bring it to the mouth. If 'a tree of life grows from the fruits of righteousness' (cf. Rev 22:2), everyone hiding righteousness with unrighteousness will not eat from this tree.
Like one holding a dog's leash, so is the one presiding over another's judgment. Use this saying for those being voted for some unworthy ones in Jerusalem or by lot (cf. Prov 27:17).
Fire flourishes in many woods; but where there is no hot-tempered one, the fight rests. He said the hot-tempered, hot-tempered one.
Smooth lips cover a sad heart. A pure heart will not seize sadness; for he has driven away corrupt desires from it.

If the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded by him. Our Satan sometimes entreats us, tickling us through unclean thoughts and throwing himself upon us with the smoothness of pleasure, and sometimes indeed raising a voice truly loud as if having been defeated, one whom one must not obey having the war against us.
For there are seven evils in his heart. These evils oppose the seven spirits.
A soul being in abundance plays with masters; but a soul in need, the bitter things seem sweet to it. A pure soul enjoys knowledge; but an unclean soul thinks false knowledge to be true knowledge.
Like a bird when it falls from its own nest, so a man is enslaved when he is made a stranger from his own places.

Virtue and knowledge are of the heart, from which being estranged a man falls into wickedness and ignorance and becomes a slave, since 'everyone practicing sin is a slave of sin' (John 8:34). The heart is delighted by perfumes, wines, and incenses; but the soul is shattered by accidents. The impassive Mind delights in diverse wisdom; but the empassioned mind will fall into ignorance.

Do not abandon your friend and your fellow-countryman; 'They have left me the spring of living water and have dug for themselves cisterns' (Jeremiah 2:13). Do not enter the house of your brother in misfortune; such was the one who entered the wedding feasts and did not have wedding clothes (Matthew 22:11). A near friend is better than a brother far from home. Better is the one joined to me through true knowledge than the one joined to me only through nature.

Take away his garment, for an insolent man passes by who plunders what belongs to others. This is that which is said in the Gospel: 'And from him who has not, even what he seems to have will be taken away' (Luke 16:34). This shows, in my opinion, the intellectual remnants of virtues and the knowledge of God being taken from men who have used them badly.

He who plants a fig tree will eat its fruits; but he who guards his Lord will be honored. Our Lord is the fig tree; for its fruit heals leprosy. If you dishonor the fool in the midst of a sitting, you will not escape his foolishness. Not dishonoring the fool will not turn him from his foolishness, but rather you are teaching him what kind of dishonor foolishness brings to a stranger.

Knowingly recognize the souls of your flock and understand your heart with your wise flocks; for they do not hand over strength and power to a man for an age, nor from generation to generation. Attend to yourself and direct your virtues, for men do not always prevail in them, nor do they transition healthily from virtue to virtue or from knowledge to knowledge, as the human condition does not easily receive this. Since he speaks of generations regarding virtues and knowledges, according to which the saints are born, he shows through what he writes: 'A generation of wisdom, the fear of the Lord, and wealth and glory and life' (Psalm 112:3). And one should use...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Law, Apatheia, and the Soul
english: By this proverb, it applies also to the shepherds of the churches, whom it is necessary to attend not to faces, but to hearts, and to shepherd the sheep intellectually.

Regarding the one who cares for the green things in the field and shears wool and gathers a pasture in the mountainous field, the mind says: the green things are the virtues existing in it according to potency, of which the one caring shears wool, being a symbol of the knowledge of God, which he again calls a mountainous pasture; for a mountainous pasture is the knowledge of holy powers fitting the irrational state of souls. It is a custom in Scripture to call holy mountains [such]. Thus also David lifts up his soul, 'From where will his help come?' (Psalm 121:1); and again: 'The mountains leap like rams, and the hills like lambs of the flock' (Psalm 114:4) concerning the salvation of Israel. For if angels rejoice over one repenting, how much more over such a multitude traveling from wickedness to virtue.

Therefore, only the knowledge of the holy angels nourishes the virtues in us, from which the soul clothes itself with the bowels of compassion, kindness, patience, humility, faith, self-control, love, and the good things generated from these. That David speaks of rational souls regarding fields, from this one can learn: 'And your fields, he says, shall be filled with fullness' (Proverbs 12:14); and again shortly after: 'And the valleys shall abound with grain; for they shall cry out and shall sing' (Psalm 65:12); for hymn and cry are by nature suited to join with the rational nature.

Regarding the man who is brave in impieties, slandering the poor like a useless and empty cloud: if he is brave in impieties, he is brave also in virtues; and if the brave man in impieties slanders the poor, the brave man in virtues exhorts the poor; surely everyone who exhorts the poor is brave in piety. Thus those abandoning the law praise impiety; but those loving the law surround themselves with a wall. Everyone who loves the law makes the...

Law: everyone practicing the law acquires apatheia and the knowledge of God. If 'those loving the law surround themselves with a wall', now the wall signifies apatheia and the knowledge of God, which alone is fit to guard the rational nature.

344 28, 7 He who guards the law is a prudent son; but he who pastures intemperance dishonors his father the Shepherd, calling the mind the shepherd, and the passions within it sheep, which he nourishes within himself, 'through the transgression of the law he dishonors God'. For intemperance of the soul is passionate thoughts being carried out through the body; but intemperance of the mind is the assumption of false dogmas and theories.

345 28, 8 He who increases his wealth through usury and excess, bringing the poor to him whom he pities—if the wealth of the ungodly is wickedness, and wise men will lose him, it is evident that the righteous and wise are losing wickedness, by means of spiritual teaching leading the impure back to virtue.

346 28, 9 He who turns his ear from not hearing the law, and he himself has detested his prayer; the law does not detest anyone's prayer, but God who gave the law. And Paul says: 'the Scripture foretelling' (Hebrews 1:1) the future, instead of 'he who gave the Scripture'.

347 28, 13 He who covers his ungodliness will not prosper; but he who explains reproofs will be loved, 'I said: I will confess my iniquity to the Lord, and you have forgiven the ungodliness of my heart' (Psalm 32:9).

348 28, 15 A hungry lion and a thirsty wolf who tyrannizes, being poor, of a needy nation; if 'blessed' (Matthew 5:6) are 'those who hunger and thirst for righteousness', lions and wolves are those who hunger and thirst for injustice.

349 28, 16 A needy king is a great slanderer; but he who hates injustice will live a long time. The approaches of the evil king are wickednesses and false dogmas; for these approach him, those who are ruled by him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Exegesis of Proverbs 29
english: A man who guarantees a murderer will be a fugitive and will not be in safety. He who guarantees Satan guarantees injustice, promising to pay him the fruits of injustice. Concerning this, the Gospel also says that one defiled through murder and strife is put into prison.
Bring up a son and he will love you and give wealth to your soul (Proverbs 28:17); he will not obey a lawless nation. A lawless nation is the order of demons, which the brought-up son does not obey.

He who works his own land will be filled with bread; but he who pursues leisure will be filled with want (Proverbs 28:19). He who purifies himself will be filled with knowledge; but the unclean will be filled with ignorance.

He who is not ashamed before the faces of the righteous is not good; such a man will be given a crust of bread instead of a man (Proverbs 28:21). If the virtues are the faces of the righteous, he is not good who is not ashamed of the virtues. And if the vices are the faces of the sinners, he is good who is not ashamed of the vices.

A wealthy man hastens to be rich, and does not know that mercy will rule him (Proverbs 28:22). Those who are now merciful will, in the age to come, be shown mercy by God and, having become angels, will rule over the ungodly. Such a status was also promised to his disciples, that the Lord would give them to sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel (Matthew 19:28). And a throne is that in which the mind sits, a spiritual knowledge gathering together those who have wandered from godliness. And to judge here means to teach, as also 'open your mouth with the word of God and judge all healthily,' instead of teaching. It is also to be understood that the merciful one, having conquered the ruler, himself will not become a ruler, but will rather make the ruler merciful.
The righteous stand in the places of the ungodly; and in their destruction the righteous will be multiplied (Proverbs 28:28). If the ungodly abandon the...

They being impious, they shall become righteous; for the destruction now signifies the removal of impiety. Thus also Matthew, having lost the tax collector, the Lord granted righteousness to him (Matt 9:13).

A man rebuking a stubborn man is better (Prov 29:1); for when he is burning, there will be no healing. He did not say that when the flame has ceased there is no healing, but that while he is burning there will be no healing, as one having wood, grass, or reed still present, even if health happens to come to those being burned after the ember.

When a righteous man is praised, peoples will rejoice; but when impious rulers rule, men groan (Prov 29:2). All those who are under the authorities and the powers and the cosmic rulers of this darkness, these certainly also groan.

A man loving wisdom, his father rejoices; but he who pastures prostitutes will lose wealth (Prov 29:3). And he who nurtures wickedness will lose knowledge. Alternatively: A good mind is a shepherd having possessed passionless thoughts, and an evil mind is a shepherd having possessed passionate thoughts. And if this is so, is not a passionate thought a goat, and is not a passionless thought a sheep? Therefore also the Lord sets the goats on the left and the sheep on the right; and he says 'goats and sheep' regarding those possessing goats and sheep, that is, those having passionate and passionless thoughts. In the same way, regarding those having the weeds, he commanded 'weeds', and regarding those having the grain, 'grain', naming them from the most inferior and most excellent state. Such is also what is said by Paul, 'love does not wander' (1 Cor 13:7), instead of 'he who has love'.
A righteous king lifts up a land; but an unlawful man overthrows it (Prov 29:4). Christ lifts up the rational nature; but the antichrist overthrows it.
A righteous man knows how to judge the poor; but the impious will not understand (Prov 29:7).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Law, Confession, and Courage
english: A discerning mind does not exist even for a poor man. Truly, he who lacks a discerning mind is poor.

A wise man judges nations; but a foolish man, being enraged, is laughed at and does not fall. 'And at him, says David, they shall laugh and say: Behold a man who did not set God as his helper' (Ps 71:10).
Men sharing in blood will seek the holy; but the upright will seek his soul. He who seeks the soul of the righteous is the one desiring to understand things as they have been thought.

A fool pours out his whole passion; but a wise man stores up [his passion] in measure. This one stores up his passion in measure, that is, he who is enraged at things concerning the righteous, or he who consumes his passion in measure through long-suffering. And to the simpler ones, one should speak the former, but to the serious ones, the latter.

An interpreter shall not exist for a nation that is lawless; but he who keeps the law is blessed. To those who have kept the law, an interpreter shall exist; but to those who have acted lawlessly, an interpreter shall not exist, but a punisher shall exist; if not by word, then by rod; a rod is given to a lawless nation.

A harsh servant will not be instructed by words; for even if he understands, he will not obey. Because no one is harsh by nature, he demonstrates 'for even if he understands, he will not obey'; for the one who is harsh by nature could never understand anything right. I say this because of Pharaoh, having been hardened against Israel, being instructed not by words, but by scourging.

He who squanders from childhood will be a servant; but at the last he will grieve for himself. If squandering makes one sin, 'for everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin' (Rom 6:16), then everyone who squanders is a slave of sin.
Pride humbles a man; but the humble-minded, the Lord exalts with glory. Now the evil pride of the soul...
He calls it logical. He who divides [the truth] is hated by his own soul. 'The thief,' he says, 'does not come except in order to steal and slaughter and destroy' (John 10:10).

If, however, having an oath set forth, they hear [it] and do not disclose [the sin], they will be turned aside by fear and shame of men. The Oath spoke the law; for just as the oath places God in the soul, so also the law introduces God into the soul; and in whatever way perjury again annuls God from the soul, so also lawlessness casts God out from it. If, therefore, he says, having heard the law set forth, they do not confess their sins, 'they will be turned aside by fear and shame of men.' Thus also David says: 'I swore and I stood to keep your judgments of righteousness' (Psalm 119:160). And again Solomon says: 'He who covers his impiety will not prosper; but he who explains and reproves will be loved' (Proverbs 28:13). And David: 'I said, he says, I will confess to the Lord my iniquity, and you forgave the impiety of my heart' (Psalm 32:5); and 'speak first of your iniquities.'

Many treat the faces of leaders; but from the Lord, justice happens to the man. In acting rightly, we treat the angels; for they are our leaders having taken us from the beginning, 'when the Most High divided the nations' (Deut 32:8) and 'he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of his angels' (Deut 32:8). And the justice from the judgment will be for us from the Lord on that day when he judges the inhabited world in righteousness (Acts 17:31), if indeed the Father has given all judgment to the Son.

What man will find a courageous woman? Courage is an excellent state of the logical soul, by which he has mastered the opposing forces of enemies. Such a thing will not fail good dogs. We plunder the opposing power having conquered.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Scholia on Proverbs
english: Those learning the words about her. She makes unserviceable wool and linen with her hands. The soul is a weaver of wool and linen, exercising the discourses concerning the animated and the unanimated, or examining the discourses concerning the practical and the natural. One said that the soul weaves wool and linen, drawing the contemplation of bodies and incorporeals toward it through the practical life.

The one who is the sun of justice finds the soul rising from the night, being watchful, and moreover praying, so that she might not fall into temptation; for she herself hastens to say, 'I awoke and became like a sparrow perching on a roof' (Psalm 84:3). She rose up and realized that it is good to work, and the lamp is not extinguished through the whole night. A pure mind is a lamp, filled with spiritual contemplation.

She stretches out her hands toward what is profitable; her shuttles she rests upon a loom. A pure mind is a loom, weaving virtue with virtue and doctrine with doctrine, or a spoken word drawing spiritual contemplation from the mind. Her husband does not care about those in the house whenever she is busy; for all those near her are being clothed. The mind would not proceed, nor would contemplation of the incorporeals occur, without first correcting the inner things; for the disturbance of the household is wont to turn it back toward those things from which it had departed. But having acquired apatheia, she will be busy in contemplation and will not care about those in the house; for the soul has clothed itself in practicalness and humility, and in desire, temperance and self-control.
She made two shuttles for her husband; garments of earth and sea from fine linen and purple. The discourses are garments of the rational soul from fine linen and...
A purple garment. Another says that the contemplation of events and the contemplation of the Holy Trinity is a garment of a pure mind made of the deep and purple.

He made linen and gave it, and girdles to the Canaanites (Proverbs 31:24). The linen shown on the roof was a symbol to Peter of the sensible world; for the various animals contained in it showed the diverse characters of men, having been purified by the cross of Christ. If one linen signified this world, may it not be that many linens contain the contemplation of various worlds, which the pure soul having contemplated, shared with others. And if the Canaanites are interpreted as the lowly, it is well that he did not give the linens to the lowly in mind, but to the pure the linens, and to the Canaanites the girdles, which are symbols of the practical life, the passionate part of the soul binding.

Narrow dwellings of the house (Proverbs 31:27). If the devil is 'king' of 'all those in the waters' and 'through waterless places he finds no rest', then it is rightly said that the narrow dwellings are the habits of the pure soul.
She was lazy and did not eat grain (Proverbs 31:27). They say that lazy grain is the evil.

For a wise woman is blessed; but the fear of the Lord let her praise (Proverbs 31:30). If 'the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom', then the soul which happens to find wisdom rightly praises the fear of the Lord, which has become to her a precursor of such knowledge.

He who does not conduct himself with his own house will inherit wind, and he will serve a fool despite being wise (Proverbs 11:29). This exhortation of the fool. Every worthless fool, every fool is a slave, therefore every worthless person is a slave.
Friends will hate poor friends, but many friends of the rich (Proverbs 14:20). For the holy angels love the holy because of their virtues; but they hate the sinners because of their poverty.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
